chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Ibn Bukayr, from Ubayd ibn Zurara, who said:
I heard Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) saying: 'Usury (Riba) does not occur except in what is measured by volume or weighed.'

key_terms.أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ: Title for Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (peace be upon him)
key_terms.الرِّبَا: Usury or interest, the core subject of the ruling
key_terms.يُكَالُ: Is measured by volume (e.g., grains, liquids)

ai.seo_question: What types of goods are subject to Riba according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from Ubayd ibn Zurara, a key narrator in the chain of al-Kulayni, establishes the principle of 'Tas'ib' (proportionality) by limiting Riba to commodities measured by volume or weight, such as grains and metals. This distinction is foundational in Shia fiqh for determining which goods are subject to the strict rules of 'Riba al-Fadl' (excess in exchange) versus general market transactions. It clarifies that not all trade involves usury, thereby providing legal clarity for commercial activities in Islamic society.

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Ibn Bukeyr, from Ubeyd Bin Zurara who said,
‘I heard Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> saying: ‘The interest does not happen to be except in what is measured or weighed’.
en.sarwar: 10. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from ibn Faddal from ibn Bukayr from ‘Ubayd ibn Zurarah who has said the following: “
I once heard abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, saying, ‘Riba’ comes in existence only in what is measured or is weighed.”
